title: Instruction
definition: An instruction is an explicitly represented operation whose permitted effect is defined by an execution model.
purpose: Establish the smallest inspectable operation used in program and algorithm reasoning.
history: Instruction representations differ across human procedures, programming languages, virtual machines, and processors; the shared curriculum idea is explicit operation and defined effect.
mental_model: An instruction names one operation and the state transition it is allowed to cause.
analogy: A precise board-game move has permitted effects under game rules; unlike a human player, a machine must not infer an unstated move.
real_world_usage: Tracing program behavior step by step
Reviewing whether an operation has a defined effect
common_mistakes: Writing several ambiguous actions as one instruction
industry_notes: Precise operations improve reviewability, test derivation, and failure isolation.
ai_notes: AI-produced steps must still be checked for ambiguity, ordering, and permitted effects.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to turn an ambiguous action into explicit ordered instructions.
exercise_candidates: Rewrite ambiguous everyday steps as explicit operations
lab_candidates: Trace the effects of a small instruction sequence
project_candidates: Create instruction cards for a simulator
